chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Muhammad ibn Isa, from Al-Husayn ibn Rashid, who said:

I asked him (peace be upon him) about clothes made in Basra according to the Yemenite style, from silk and cotton. Is it permissible for the deceased to be enshrouded in them? He (peace be upon him) said: If the cotton is more than the silk, then there is no problem.

key_terms.عَمَلِ الْعَصْبِ الْيَمَانِيِّ: Yemenite style/workmanship (referring to a specific type of fabric weave)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to shroud the deceased in silk and cotton mixed fabric?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi clarifies the juristic principle of 'ghalabah' (preponderance) in determining the permissibility of mixed fabrics for shrouds, specifically addressing the Basran practice of blending silk (qazz) with cotton. It reflects the Shia scholarly consensus that the dominant material dictates the ruling, ensuring that the shroud remains pure and suitable for burial, thereby avoiding the prohibition associated with excessive silk.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Muhammad Bin Ahmad, from Muhammad Bin Isa, from Al Husayn Bin Rashid who said,

‘I asked him<sup>asws</sup> about the clothes made in Al-Basra upon Yemenite workmanship from silk and cotton. Is it correct for the deceased to be enshrouded in it?’ He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘When it was more cotton that the silk, so there is no problem’.
en.sarwar: 12. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Muhammad ibn Ahmad from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from al-Husayn ibn Rashid who has said the following: “I once asked him (the Imam), ‘Alayhi al-Salam, about the fabrics made in al-Basrah in the form of Yemenite workmanship out of silk or cotton if it can be used to shroud a deceased? He (the Imam) said, ‘If the amount of cotton in the fabric is more than the amount of silk, then it is permissible to use it for shrouding.’”
